frontier.hypothesis: There is a refs lever that is not loop_depth: a construct that gives a pseudo a mention surviving to flow.c's reg_n_refs accumulation while emitting no instruction, which would move the arg5 value from 4 refs to 5 or 6 with zero loop notes and close the tie on the g06 order-perfect base.
frontier.mechanism: qty_compare_1's only free input on an order-perfect base is qty_n_refs (H-s69-C). loop_depth is dead (H-s69-D: notes are sched1 region boundaries here) and self-copies are dead (H-s69-E: delete_noop_moves precedes the counter). What has never been enumerated is which OTHER RTL positions flow.c counts - a mention inside a REG_EQUAL/REG_NOTE, a use consumed by a combine merge, or a second use folded into the addressing mode of an insn that already exists.
frontier.next_probe: Read flow.c's reg_n_refs accumulation loop first and list exactly which rtx positions it walks (does it count REG_NOTES? does it count uses inside a MEM address?). Then spell one C form per counted-but-instruction-free position on the g06 base and re-dump with BB2_QTY_DEBUG, checking refs(reg97) before checking the score.

frontier.hypothesis: A loop note placed OUTSIDE block 3 - both its BEG and END in the predecessor block - raises block 3's loop_depth without introducing a scheduling-region boundary inside block 3, giving the refs change without the order damage that killed H-s69-D.
frontier.mechanism: s67-A and H-s69-D both show the damage comes from the note acting as a sched1 region boundary INSIDE the block being scheduled. Every wrap measured in 69 sessions has been placed inside the do_timeout block. flow.c's loop_depth is a running counter over the whole insn stream, so a BEG in an earlier block that is closed after block 3 would raise block 3's depth with no note between block 3's own insns.
frontier.next_probe: Wrap from before the do_timeout label (or from the loop head) through the end of the do_timeout block in a do-while(0), so both notes land outside block 3's insn range; measure the score, then dump BB2_QTY_DEBUG and check whether refs in block 3 doubled while the block-3 RANKDBG stream is unchanged.
